headline: Two held over 11 sheep taken from Korgoncho pen; nine recovered
dek: Police traced a pick-up to a yard on the edge of Bazar-Korgon, where nine animals were found; two are believed sold.
paragraphs: Police in Lower Naryn District detained two men on Tuesday over the theft of 11 sheep from a farmstead pen in Korgoncho, the Iyık Janyl City Police press service said.

According to Maj. Shavkat Yuldashev, the press officer, the animals were taken on the night of Sunday 15 to Monday 16 November. The owner, a local farmer, found the pen empty and its gate lifted off its hinges on Monday morning and reported the loss to the Ministry of Internal Security's Lower Naryn detachment.
Officers traced a pick-up to a yard on the edge of Bazar-Korgon, where nine of the 11 sheep were recovered. The other two are believed to have been sold. Major Yuldashev said no one was hurt.

A 29-year-old Korgoncho resident (born 1997, K.R.) and a 33-year-old Bazar-Korgon resident (born 1993, A.T.) are held on suspicion of theft of livestock committed by prior agreement under the Criminal Code. The press service said the investigation continues and that the two sold animals are still being sought.
For the owner the loss is partly made good: nine of 11 animals are back. Stock in the district is usually sold at the Sunday livestock market at Bazar-Korgon, which opens at dawn.
